<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **8** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **26** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c1240a38ac2c23c8d526e476a20edeabbbefd6f6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f13607b3d76935a7595fbeeefa033155b4a4b8b1` — the merge of head `8767d6aa81725636037589b29b3ad59a9b4a37e9` into base `c1240a38ac2c23c8d526e476a20edeabbbefd6f6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f13607b3d76935a7595fbeeefa033155b4a4b8b1 && git checkout f13607b3d76935a7595fbeeefa033155b4a4b8b1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c1240a38ac2c23c8d526e476a20edeabbbefd6f6 8767d6aa81725636037589b29b3ad59a9b4a37e9 && git checkout -B drift-repro c1240a38ac2c23c8d526e476a20edeabbbefd6f6 && git merge --no-ff 8767d6aa81725636037589b29b3ad59a9b4a37e9

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c1240a38ac2c23c8d526e476a20edeabbbefd6f6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c1240a38ac2c23c8d526e476a20edeabbbefd6f6` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `89ff3aa9e1d941b2a20ed3c33ebc13c81ea18f55`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/allowed-ip-ranges.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/allowed-ip-ranges.pin.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/index.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-routes.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service.types.ts, .changeset/30203-allowed-ip-ranges-live.md + packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/client-address.ts (the trust rule), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts (`ipMatchesRange`, `unmapIpv4`, `isClientIpAllowed`, `resolveClientAddress`, `applyConfigPatch`), the sign-in gate and the per-piece application in auth-plugin.ts (the `registerAuthRoutes` D5 block and `applyPiece`), packages/services/service-settings/src/manifests/auth.manifest.ts (`allowed_ip_ranges`, scope global), `effectiveEnvOverride` / `coerceEnvValue` / `registerWritePredicate` / `setMany` pre-flight in settings-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/adapter.ts (`readRemoteAddress`), packages/spec/src/contracts/http-server.ts (`remoteAddress`), docs/adr/0069-enterprise-authentication-hardening.md D5, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs and scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs (for ②), and PR #30298 at `249ec4c4` (for ③). Inputs: card #30203 body and comments 6648444250, 6649086146, 6650755695; PR body, file list, net diff `origin/main...89ff3aa9` (8 files, +507 / -12); the head's check-runs.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Which doors are judged — right.** The predicate runs inside `SettingsService.setMany` (`refuseByWritePredicates`, after the declared constraints, before any row) and judges only when the input carries `transport`. The only producer of `transport` is the `PUT /api/settings/:namespace` route, which always sets it (headers always; `remoteAddress` when the adapter has one). So: the console save is judged; an in-process `set` / `setMany` (boot, seed, migration, an `auth:configure` host, `resetNamespace`) carries no request and is let through; a `null` (clear) returns before any address is read. A boot or non-request write must be neither refused nor skipped: there is no caller connection to lock out, and refusing one would brick a seeded deployment. Correct. A request write that is not the console — an IaC runner or a CLI calling the REST door from a host outside the list — IS refused; that is the rule applied honestly (the gate would refuse that host too), and the refusal names the recovery.
- **Clearing semantics — right.** `declaredAllowedIpRanges` is captured at init after `ctx.trigger('auth:configure', authConfig)` (so a host handler's list counts), and the `else if (this.allowedIpRangesFromSettings)` branch only emits a patch when the running list came from a stored setting, so a deployment that never stored one sees no extra patch. The reset rides the non-refusable `patch` piece, `applyConfigPatch` spreads `allowedIpRanges` whole, and `isClientIpAllowed` reads an empty array as open. A cleared value with a deployment-declared list returns to that list, not to none (pinned). `isExplicit` is untouched, so the sibling keys keep the old behaviour, reported in ③.
- **The env pin — right.** `OS_AUTH_ALLOWED_IP_RANGES=''` is a string in `this.env`, `coerceEnvValue` hands it back unchanged for a textarea, the key resolves `source: 'env'`, `isExplicit` is true, `parseAllowedIpRanges('')` is `[]`, the gate opens (pinned). While pinned the key is `locked`, so the console save is refused `409 SETTINGS_LOCKED` in the pre-flight, before any predicate.
- **The new public surface — the declaration is WRONG.** `@objectstack/service-settings` is a published package (`private` unset, 18.3.0). This head adds two exports to its `index.ts` (`SettingsWriteOptions`, `SettingsRequestTransport`), widens `setMany`'s fourth parameter from `SettingsDisplayOptions` to `SettingsWriteOptions`, and adds `transport` to `SettingsWritePredicateInput`, the input every predicate author reads. That is a purely additive widening of a published package's public surface — the question the `Clause-②:` line answers (扩大公开面吗) — and the dispatch itself said `yes` for new published code. The PR body and the changeset declare `no (narrowing)` and say "nothing is widened", while the same changeset's fourth bullet describes exactly this widening. The honest line is `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`: a diff that widens one surface (the settings write seam) and narrows another (the console save). Under ruling A the level is decoupled from this line, so `patch` stays correct with `Metadata-protocol: none`; the narrowing arm keeps this review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Must-fix (see ②).

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/30203-allowed-ip-ranges-live.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-auth: patch`, `@objectstack/service-settings: patch`. Level right: `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`; a non-protocol narrowing ships `patch` with its BREAKING banner (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3, ruling A). The `**BREAKING**` banner is present and states who moves and how; the ADR-0087 marker is present, disposition `not-required`, category `no-migration-prescription`, and the body carries no FROM → TO prescription (the "Who moves" bullet is prose, no arrow and no table), so the category holds. `Check Changeset` and the lint gate that runs the ADR-0087 registration are green on this head.
- Declaration lines: `Clause-②:` and `Metadata-protocol:` are byte-identical between the PR body and the changeset. Both are wrong in the same way (① last bullet). **Must-fix:** rewrite the line in BOTH places to `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` with reasoning that names the widened surface (the two new `service-settings` exports, the `setMany` options and the predicate input) and the narrowed one (the console save); keep `Metadata-protocol: none` and both `patch` levels. A `yes` with `none` and `patch` is the shape ruling A made legal; nothing else in the changeset needs to move.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Four `service-settings` files outside the claimed surface** (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/` plus a changeset): read and accepted as necessary — the save door had no way to carry the caller's connection to a predicate, the extension is additive and optional, no `packages/spec` change, no new error code, settings key or env var. Accepted here as a declared deviation; its consequence is the ② correction above, not a reversal.
- **Manifest help text unchanged**: accepted. The `allowed_ip_ranges` description already states the trust-proxy rule; the refusal text carries the self-lockout lesson. The docs half (`content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`: refusal and `OS_AUTH_ALLOWED_IP_RANGES` recovery) and the console half (show the caller's address before saving, read `constraint.clientAddress`) are named for the seat; both must become cards, not stay as notes.
- **Full dogfood red on `permission-set-clone-door.dogfood.test.ts`**: read as main-caused (#30222 grants on `sys_comment` / `sys_activity`); nothing in this diff touches permission sets, metadata validation or the clone door. The seat's out-of-scope list names it with dedupe words; it is a class-a defect and must be filed as a card under the main-red convention, not left as a note.
- **The clear-skips family** (`lockout_threshold`, `max_concurrent_sessions_per_user`, every `if (isExplicit(key))` branch without a reset): a reproducible defect measured on the real composition; Prime Directive #10 says file it. The report carries it as an out-of-scope finding with dedupe words; the seat files the card. Scope choice (this key only) is accepted: the general fix crosses the `refusable` pieces #30201 / #30202 are editing.
- **Composition with PR #30298 (card #30202, same seat), read at its head `249ec4c4`:** its diff touches `auth-plugin.ts` only at the top of `bindAuthSettings` (one import, one `registerSignInMethodFloor(settings, …)` call) and no `service-settings` file; this PR's `auth-plugin.ts` hunks are the `SettingsReadSurface` member, two fields, the `declaredAllowedIpRanges` capture, the `allowed_ip_ranges` branch and the predicate registration before `applySettings()`. Disjoint lines, both register predicates on different keys through the same last-wins-per-key seam: textual merge clean, semantics compose. **Conflict risk, flagged:** #30298's body names a `batch` field on `SettingsWritePredicateInput` as a possible follow-up. If it is added, the types file grows next to the `transport?` member this PR adds (same hunk region) and the predicate call in `refuseByWritePredicates` — which this PR reshapes into a multi-line object literal — is the line both would edit; whichever lands second takes a rebase there. Both fields being optional, the two compose once rebased. No ruling needed.
- Open questions in the os-dev-report: none declared; none found.

### ④ Design judgment

Judged on the tree, against the sign-in gate and the settings service as cited.

- **Same address on both doors — holds.** The sign-in gate resolves `mgr.resolveClientAddress({ headers, ...transportOf(c) })` and judges `isClientIpAllowed`; the predicate resolves `mgr.resolveClientAddress({ headers, remoteAddress })` from the route's `req.headers` / `req.remoteAddress` and judges `ipMatchesRange`. Both read `trustProxy` live from the manager's config, both read the same forwarded-header list (`client-address.ts`, leftmost `X-Forwarded-For`, then `X-Real-IP`, believed only under `trustProxy`), and the hono adapter fills `IHttpRequest.remoteAddress` from the same socket `readRemoteAddress` reads. `trustProxy` off: the proxy's address is judged at both doors (so an admin behind an untrusted proxy saving the office range is refused, naming the proxy address — correct, that is the deployment's bug and the gate would refuse the same). `trustProxy` on: the forwarded client address at both. Pinned both ways.
- **Undetermined address — holds.** `resolveClientAddress` returns `undefined` when neither fact exists; the gate refuses such a request while any list is set; the predicate refuses any non-empty list with `clientAddress: null` and the `undetermined` copy. Consistent; pinned.
- **IPv4-mapped / IPv6.** `unmapIpv4` folds `::ffff:a.b.c.d` on both sides, so a dual-stack peer saves and signs in against an IPv4 range (pinned with `::ffff:127.0.0.1`). Plain IPv6 matches exact-only on both doors, and an IPv6 CIDR never matches anywhere (`ipMatchesRange` falls back to exact match when either side is not IPv4) — a pre-existing gate limitation, now consistently applied at the save. **Should-fix:** the `outside` copy says the list "does not include" the address; for an admin at `2001:db8::1` saving `2001:db8::/32` the list does include it textually and the matcher cannot read it. Word it as "does not match" or name the matcher's reach (IPv4 CIDR and exact addresses), and file the IPv6-CIDR gap as a card against the gate (the manifest description promises "CIDR ranges" unqualified).
- **CIDR parsing errors — no crash path.** `parseAllowedIpRanges` splits and trims only; `ipMatchesRange` never throws (`/33`, a non-numeric prefix or a hostname fall to exact match). A malformed-only list is refused at the save because nothing can match the caller — a protective side effect, not validation; a mixed list saves with the malformed entry inert, as before. Pre-existing; no finding against this PR.
- **Non-HTTP contexts — allowed, by construction.** No `transport` ⇒ `undefined` before any read; no `authManager` yet ⇒ `undefined`. Nothing crashes. The only in-tree in-process writers of settings outside this package write other keys. Right.
- **Env-pinned key and restore-default.** Covered in ①: a locked key refuses `409` before predicates; `resetNamespace` and a `null` save both resolve `default`, fire the subscription, and the else-branch returns the gate to the declared list (pinned).
- **Forging `transport` — not reachable.** `transport` is the route's fourth argument to `setMany`, never read from the body; a body key `transport` (or `values.transport`) is an unknown key and the pre-flight refuses the batch `400 UNKNOWN_KEY`. A spoofed `X-Forwarded-For` is believed only under `trustProxy`, exactly as the gate believes it; the caller already holds `manage_platform_settings`, so the check is a self-lockout belt, not an authorization control — and it is spelled so in the types. Right.
- **Should-fix (information flow):** `SettingsRequestTransport.headers` hands the ENTIRE header map — `cookie`, `authorization`, API keys — to every write predicate any plugin registers, while the only consumer reads the forwarded-address family. Narrow what the route forwards to the forwarded-address headers (or document in the TSDoc that a predicate receives credential-bearing headers and must not log or store them). The current TSDoc says the transport "is never stored or logged"; nothing enforces that on a predicate author.
- **Should-fix (nit):** `SettingsReadSurface.registerWritePredicate?` takes its `input` as `any`; `unknown` with the structural `AllowedIpRangesWriteInput` pick keeps plugin-auth free of a `service-settings` type dependency without an `any`.
- Tests: the pin boots the real `AuthPlugin`, the real `SettingsService` with the shipped auth manifest and the real settings routes through the vitest alias; `@objectstack/service-settings` is a workspace devDependency of plugin-auth, so the file runs in Test Core. Nine cases cover each branch the four ablations name. Good.
- Degradation levels: the predicate-registration `catch` logs `warn` (functional: the belt is missing, the gate still enforces) — right level.

**Check-runs on `89ff3aa9`** (polled every two minutes from 05:47 to 05:57 UTC, the ten-minute cap): green — `Lint & Repo Gates` and every `Lint ·` lane, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Test Core (2/8, 5/8, 6/8, 7/8, 8/8)`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Build Core`, `Test UI`, `Live E2E UI`, the PR-body guards. Still `in_progress` at the last poll: `Test Core (1/8, 3/8, 4/8)`. No red on this head; judged with what is there. The verdict below does not depend on them: it is decided by the declaration defect in ②.

**Findings**

- MUST-FIX (①/②): `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is false on the tree — `@objectstack/service-settings` gains two published exports, a widened `setMany` options type and a new predicate-input field; declare `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` identically in the PR body and the changeset, levels and `Metadata-protocol: none` unchanged.
- SHOULD-FIX (④): forward only the forwarded-address headers in `SettingsRequestTransport`, or state in its TSDoc that predicates receive credential-bearing headers.
- SHOULD-FIX (④): the `outside` refusal copy should say "does not match" (or name the matcher's IPv4-CIDR / exact reach); file the IPv6-CIDR gap on the gate as a card.
- SHOULD-FIX (④, nit): `registerWritePredicate?` on `SettingsReadSurface` takes `unknown`, not `any`.
- SEAT (③): file the clear-skips family and the #30222 dogfood red as cards; name the docs and console halves as cards.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8767d6aa81725636037589b29b3ad59a9b4a37e9`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/allowed-ip-ranges.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/index.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-routes.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-service.types.ts, packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-write-predicate-transport.test.ts, .changeset/30203-allowed-ip-ranges-live.md + packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/client-address.ts (`resolveClientAddress`, `firstHeader`), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/client-address-forwarding.ts (`FORWARDED_CLIENT_ADDRESS_HEADERS`), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/client-address-vendor.ts (the vendored reader's one header), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts (`resolveClientAddress`, `ipMatchesRange`, `isClientIpAllowed`), the D5 gate block and `transportOf` in auth-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/allowed-ip-ranges.pin.test.ts (unchanged by the delta; the trustProxy case), packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/adapter.ts (`rawHeaders = c.req.header()`, `readRemoteAddress`), packages/spec/src/contracts/http-server.ts (`IHttpRequest.headers`, `remoteAddress`), packages/services/service-settings/src/localization-currency-lock.ts and settings-write-predicate.test.ts (the other `registerWritePredicate` callers), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/index.ts and package.json (whether the new module is republished), PR #30298 at `249ec4c4` (for ③), cards #30320 and #30255 (for ③). Inputs: card #30203 body and comments 6648444250, 6649086146, 6650755695, 6650829184; PR #30309 body as replaced at 06:58 UTC, file list (9 files, +679 / -18 against `main`), the net diff `origin/main...8767d6aa`, the delta `89ff3aa9..8767d6aa` (one commit, 8 files, +191 / -25; no `main` merge in the range); record 6650936040; the check-runs on this head. This record reviews the DELTA against record 6650936040; the judgments of that record on the unchanged parts stand and are not restated.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The delta, hunk by hunk.** (a) `settings-service.ts`: the predicate registry now stores `{ predicate, requestHeaders }` per key, `registerWritePredicate` takes an optional fourth `options` whose `requestHeaders` are lower-cased into a `Set` at registration, and `refuseByWritePredicates` hands each predicate `narrowTransport(display.transport, registered.requestHeaders)` instead of the whole transport. `narrowTransport` copies only the header entries whose lower-cased name is in the set, under their incoming spelling, plus `remoteAddress` when present; it builds a fresh object per predicate, so no predicate can mutate what a sibling sees. (b) `settings-service.types.ts`: new `SettingsWritePredicateOptions`, and `SettingsWritePredicateInput.transport`'s TSDoc now states the narrowing. (c) `index.ts`: `SettingsWritePredicateOptions` exported. (d) `settings-routes.ts`: comment only; the route still hands the full `req.headers` and `req.remoteAddress` to the service, which is right: narrowing per predicate has to happen where the registrations are known. (e) `auth-plugin.ts`: the structural `SettingsReadSurface.registerWritePredicate?` takes `input: unknown` and an optional `options`, and the registration names `FORWARDED_CLIENT_ADDRESS_HEADERS`. (f) `allowed-ip-ranges.ts`: the predicate's parameter is `unknown`, read structurally through `AllowedIpRangesWriteInput`; the `outside` copy in all four locales says no entry matches. (g) the new `settings-write-predicate-transport.test.ts`, three cases. (h) the changeset's declaration and prose. Judged on the tree, trying to break `narrowTransport` and the per-predicate header contract against the gate it must agree with.

- **Header-name case — holds.** Registration lower-cases every name (`new Set(names.map(toLowerCase))`); `narrowTransport` compares `name.toLowerCase()` of each incoming key against that set and keeps the incoming spelling. So `requestHeaders: ['X-Forwarded-For', 'x-real-ip']` against lower-case incoming keys matches (pinned in the new test, first case). Both doors take their header map from Hono's `c.req.header()`: the gate directly (D5 block, auth-plugin.ts), the save through the hono adapter's `rawHeaders = c.req.header()` into `IHttpRequest.headers`; Hono lower-cases keys, and the list is lower-case, so every lookup lines up. The one spelling that would not match is an adapter delivering mixed-case keys: `narrowTransport` would still pass them through (it matches case-insensitively), but `resolveClientAddress`'s `firstHeader` reads `headers[name] ?? headers[name.toLowerCase()]` with a lower-case `name`, so it would miss them at the gate and at the save alike. Same answer at both doors is what the rule requires; no finding against this delta.
- **Coverage of the forwarded headers — complete by construction.** `resolveClientAddress` reads forwarded headers only inside `for (const name of FORWARDED_CLIENT_ADDRESS_HEADERS)`, and the plugin registers that very constant, so the predicate receives every header the address rule can read (`x-forwarded-for`, `x-real-ip`) and no other. No `Forwarded`, `CF-Connecting-IP` or `True-Client-IP` reader exists in plugin-auth, the runtime or the hono adapter (grepped); the vendored library reads only the platform-written `x-objectstack-client-address`, which the platform sets from the already-resolved address, never from the client. If a later change widens the rule's list, the registration widens with it, because it names the list and not two literals. The save and the gate therefore judge the same address under `trustProxy` on and off. Ablation E in the body (registering `[]`) reds exactly the trustProxy case, which is the failure shape a missing header would produce; the pin would catch a drift.
- **A predicate with no `requestHeaders` — receives `headers: {}` and the peer address** (pinned, second case). This is the right default: the peer address is the one fact a client cannot forge, and a predicate that wants a header says so where its registration can be audited. The currency-lock predicate is such a one and reads neither.

Ablation F (pass every header) reds both header cases.
